title: HEIRS: Hybrid Three-Dimension RRAM- and SRAM-CIM Architecture for Multi-task Transformer Acceleration
problem: RRAM-CIM suffers from expensive weight rewrites when handling dynamic/tuned weights in transfer learning, while pure SRAM-CIM cannot efficiently store large models at scale. Current hybrid CIM architectures cannot properly support cooperative weight addition from both shared and tuned weights.
motivation: Efficient hardware acceleration of large-scale transformers with multi-task transfer learning deployment requires overcoming memory bottlenecks while maintaining support for dynamic weight updates.
method: HEIRS combines two types of memory in 3D: an RRAM layer (dense memory that stores large amounts of data but uses significant power to rewrite) that holds the entire base model, and an SRAM layer (fast memory optimized for frequent updates) that handles task-specific weight changes without triggering rewrites in the RRAM. The SRAM layer performs matrix-vector multiplication (the core computation where weight rows multiply with input vectors) on the dynamic weights. An input selective adder tree then combines results from both layers, letting shared base weights and task-specific tuned weights work together.
key_novelty: 3D stacking of RRAM and SRAM with an input selective adder tree eliminates the expensive weight-rewriting problem in transfer learning by keeping base model weights permanently in RRAM while task-specific updates happen in SRAM.
contributions: 3D monolithic integration architecture combining ultra-high-density RRAM-CIM with high-performance SRAM-CIM for multi-task transformers
Novel hybrid-CIM paradigm with input selective adder tree enabling efficient cooperative weight addition from shared and tuned parameters
7.83x energy efficiency improvement over RRAM-CIM and 2.29x over SRAM-CIM on BERT
85.5% latency reduction and 7.2x storage density enhancement compared to RRAM-CIM
primary_theme: Hybrid CIM architecture for efficient multi-task transformer acceleration
